chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man who asked Al-Maazy (peace be upon him) about the prayer in foxes.

He forbade from the prayer in it and in the garment that is underneath it. So I did not know which of the two garments was the one that sticks to the fur or the one that sticks to the skin. So he (peace be upon him) signed by his handwriting: 'The one that sticks to the skin'.
He said, 'And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) mentioned that he was asked about this matter, so he said: 'Do not pray in the garment that is above it, nor in the one that is underneath it'.

key_terms.الْمَاضِيَ: The Late Imam (referring to the 7th Imam Musa al-Kazim)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in fur clothing according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of *khafaf* (fur) garments, distinguishing between the hair side and the leather side to determine ritual purity. While the initial report suggests avoiding the layer touching the skin, the later clarification by Imam al-Rida (or another Imam, depending on the specific chain interpretation) extends the precaution to both layers, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing doubt (*shakk*) in acts of worship. This highlights the practical application of *istishab* and *takhayyur* in determining the purity of materials derived from animals.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, (It has been narrated) from a man who asked Al-Maazyasws (7th Imamasws), about the Salāt in the foxes (furs), but heasws forbade from performing Salāt in it, and in the clothes which are underneath it. So I did not know which of the two clothes – the one which touches the fur or that which touches with the skin. So heasws signed by hisasws handwriting: ‘That which touches with the skin’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Al-Hassanasws mentioned that heasws was asked about this problem, so heasws said: ‘You cannot pray Salāt in the cloth which is above it, nor in that which is underneath it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar from a man who had has said the following: “He had asked him (the Imam) about performing Salah (prayer) with foxes (things from it) and he (the Imam) prohibited him to perform Salah (prayer) in such things and with the clothes which is the next layer. He (the man) did not know which layer was meant; the one touching the furs or the one touching one’s skin. He (the Imam) wrote with his handwriting that said, ‘It is the one that touches the skin.

He (the narrator) has said that he then asked abu al-Hassan that he had asked him (the Imam) about this issue and he (the Imam) had said, ‘Do not perform Salah (prayer) with the clothes which are on its top as well as that which is beneath.’”
